reasons: Claimed status is compliant, and the finding correctly proposes no redline and no counterparty comment — the rendered redline is identical to the originals, consistent with a retained-evidence (non-negotiated) finding.

The cited text supports compliance: § 14 gives Client an at-will right to terminate on written notice (no cause, no minimum notice, no early-termination fee), with services and fees running only to the end of the following month (~30–60 days), which meets or beats the preferred 30-day convenience right without penalty.

Vendor side also meets the preferred position: § 13 fixes a 1-year auto-renewing term and TrueLink's only exit is a symmetric end-of-term non-renewal notice; the two mid-term triggers are for-cause (and partial, affecting only §§ 2–3), so there is no Vendor mid-term convenience walk-away.

Sub-elements short of the model language are correctly noted rather than flagged: no express pro-rata refund (immaterial because § 5a bills monthly in arrears, so Client does not prepay) and TrueLink's 30-day non-renewal notice versus the fallback's 90 days — a symmetric right in a 12-month (not multi-year) term that equally benefits Client, so it is not a mid-term vendor convenience right.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is a phrasing artefact: § 14 never uses the words 'for convenience' but grants an unqualified election to terminate, so the substance is present.
The drafting note on the mis-numbered cross-references to 'Section 12' (actual termination mechanic is § 14) is accurately flagged as housekeeping rather than a T4C deviation.
